outcome: Accuracy of clinical diagnosis of OASIS using endoanal ultrasound (EAUS)
Correlation between confirmed injury and change to anorectal physiology squeeze pressure
cohort: 1135 women who attended the Third- and Fourth-Degree Tears Clinic at the study institution, 12 weeks post-delivery, between June 2008 and October 2019.
finding: Of women with suspected OASIS, 21.2% did not have an injury on EAUS, while those with confirmed injury were more likely to report flatus incontinence and have reduced anal sphincter pressures.
